### Context

A local test reproduces the saved dark theme turning light. Turning off a later default-setting step kept dark.

### What is broken

After a refresh, the account page shows the light theme instead of the saved dark theme.

### Why it is broken

The page gets the saved theme from the part that supplies saved account preferences, the profile service, which returns dark. The page applies dark first. A separate step that sets a default theme then runs and replaces dark with light. A test confirmed this cause: with that later step turned off, the page kept dark.

### How to fix it

Skip the default theme step once a saved theme has loaded. A refresh should then keep dark. The fix is small and safe. Choose hotfix because the fix is small and safe.

### What is broken

Refreshing the account page resets the saved dark theme to light.

### Why it is broken

Two parts of the page set the theme: the profile loader applies the saved `"dark"` value, then the default-theme initializer overwrites it with `"light"` (`src/profile-theme.ts:62`). The local test `node --test test/profile-theme.test.mjs` reproduces the reset; disabling the later initializer keeps dark, supporting the overwrite as the cause.

### How to fix it

Skip default initialization after a saved theme has loaded so refresh retains dark. This is a small, bounded change to the initializer, with the existing local test covering the failure. Choose hotfix because the fix is small and all six eligibility predicates pass.
